Quire design system

What the desktop app is made of today, read from the code, alongside 66 tracked findings: 42 settled and 24 open (2 high, 8 medium, 14 low). Every value names the file and line it comes from. The tokens are the --q-* variables in the first style block; the components below are drawn from them, so changing a token changes every specimen.

Working on this page: keep the --q-* names, the data-component and data-issue attributes, and write each decision into its card's data-decision attribute and "Decision" line. design/system/handoff.py reads those back and writes the implementer's brief. Mark anything new with data-new.

Colour

A theme is eight colours: page, sidebar, ink, second ink, muted text, faint marks, accent, error. Every built-in theme, including Paper and Ink, derives the remaining tones through theme::build and theme::with_accent. Seven more named colours (green, red, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, orange) colour code and alerts.

Rules

Two chrome familiesThe panel family (iA Writer Quattro S, or the system monospace) is for navigation, key names and literal values. Instrument Sans is for everything else. No view sets a family itself (ui/styles.rs, test ui_builders_take_chrome_styles).
Colour by roleChrome reads the palette (Pal). The page and the side panels read roles derived from it (roles.rs), each lifted until it reads: faint text 4.5:1, rows 1.43 times that, current text 1.15 times that.
Contrast is computedAn accent is moved toward white or black until it reaches 3:1 on the page. Text on the accent is whichever of white or black reads better.
Pixel gridChrome sizes round to device pixels (theme::px); page line boxes round to whole points (page::r).
LayersLight layers (menus, drawers, layout picker) sit without a full-window modal scrim (drawers dim the page under the title bar). Heavy layers (palette, Settings, lock, trash, help, edit sheet, lightbox) sit on a full-window scrim. Every open layer traps Tab, closes on Esc or a click outside, and returns focus on close.
Focus ringNamed rings in ui/tokens.rs (FocusRing): Standard (2 wide, 3 out, ink) on controls Tab reaches, Tight (2 wide, 1 out, ink) in find bars, Input (1.5 wide, 1 inside, readable faint) on text inputs, and Inset (2 wide, 2 inside, ink) inside bordered inputs. Selected items wear the accent, so focus and selection never look alike.
One Tab stop per listTab enters a list at its current row and leaves on the next Tab. Arrows move inside. F6 and Shift+F6 move between panes.
EscCloses the nearest thing: a notice, then find, then an inline field, then the layer (clearing a non-empty query first in the palette and help search). In Source it then returns to Preview.
Keys shown to the userWritten 'Ctrl+Shift+K', modifiers in the order Ctrl, Alt, Shift. A tooltip reads 'Name (Key)'. Help lists every chord; tooltips and the palette show the first.
Pointer targetsAt least 24 × 24 (TARGETS24).
Reduced motionEvery transition becomes a jump (PAGE-84).
WordsQuire says 'note', never 'document'. Sentence case.

Inconsistencies

checked means the cited lines were read again against the code after the mapping. reported means the finding comes from a Haiku map and the lines were not read again: read them before acting.
